test_title: SSC CGL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On : 7 March 2023)
subject: general
question: At a clearance sale, a shopkeeper gives 45% discount. If a customer paid ₹330 during the sale, then what is the marked price of that shirt ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = 45% ⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100% − 45% = 55%

Given, 55% of Marked Price (MP) = ₹330

1% of MP = 330 ÷ 55 = 6

100% (MP) = 6 × 100 = ₹600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹330

Discount percentage (D%) = 45%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − D%]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b0cf3b802fc77abc608717186f65b4f88f9ee13d6211892e01f5e1a0e647a3e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP = [330 × 100] ÷ [100 − 45]

⇒ MP = 33000 ÷ 55

⇒ MP = 6600 ÷ 11

⇒ MP = 600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed on the label of an article. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price.

Successive Discount Formula

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the total effective discount = (a + b − (a × b)/100)%.

Relation between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This is used to find the markup percentage.
